prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Preset Fast-Track Adoption Flow [adoption, new_flow]: predicted +15.0%, measured +9.3% (p=0.000373), won
- round 1: Move Sign-In after Pet Adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured +4.3% (p=0.009364), won
- round 1: Spotlight Layout for Final Desktop Welcome [finish, layout]: predicted +8.0%, measured +6.1% (p=0.075164), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Background Rendering Notification Prompt [home, notification]: predicted +7.0%, measured +3.4% (p=0.092816), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Photo Quality Assistant Callout [adoption, hint]: predicted +7.0%, measured +10.2% (p=3.3e-05), won
- round 2: Existing Account Sync Assurance Banner [sign_in, copy]: predicted +4.0%, measured +1.9% (p=0.245021), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Interactive Generation Progress & Tip Carousel [home, wait_info]: predicted +3.0%, measured +7.8% (p=6.1e-05), won
- round 2: Split View Path Selection Screen [choose_path, layout]: predicted +3.0%, measured +7.9% (p=0.0), won

Previous lessons:
Fast-track adoption flows effectively improved onboarding metrics.
Reordering sign-in after pet adoption was helpful and won.
Spotlight layout changes on the final desktop welcome screen showed no clear effect.
Background rendering notification prompts showed no clear effect.
Predictions consistently overestimated the actual measured uplift across all tests.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Fast-track adoption flows and moving sign-in after pet adoption were helpful.
Photo quality callouts, interactive tip carousels, and split-view path selection screens were helpful.
Spotlight layouts on the final welcome screen, background notification prompts, and account sync copy banners showed no clear effect.
Predictions were too high for initial flow changes and non-significant tests, but were too low for visual callouts, progress carousels, and path selection screens.
